en: The Apadāna of the Elder Vatthadāyaka Sakacintaniya Chapter 7 I gave a garment to the Buddha, the Teacher, who was free from passion. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. In this fortunate aeon, I was born in the city of Bandhumatī as a king. I was known as Bandhumanta, a ruler of the four quarters, a wheel-turning monarch. I ruled over the earth, bounded by the ocean, without violence and without weapons, governing with righteousness, bringing peace and security to all beings. When I had performed great meritorious deeds, I passed away from that human life. Through the ripening of that karma, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. There, I enjoyed divine pleasures for sixty-four thousand aeons. Having lived there for a long time, I passed away from that celestial existence. In this fortunate aeon, I was born in the city of Kapilavatthu as a prince. I was known as Sakyamuni, a son of King Suddhodana. When I had reached the age of twenty-nine, I went forth from home into homelessness. For six years I practiced austerities, striving for the sake of awakening. Then, at the foot of the Bodhi tree, I attained supreme, unsurpassed enlightenment. I set rolling the Wheel of Dhamma at Isipatana in Varanasi. I established the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts among the people. I converted the multitude of disciples and established them in the Dhamma. I ordained five hundred bhikkhus and sent them forth into the world. I established the Sangha of bhikkhus and taught the path to liberation. At that time I was born as a bird,
a supaṇṇa, the lord of garuḷas;
I saw the Buddha, free from dust.
As he was going to Gandhamādana,
I abandoned my form as a garuḍa and assumed the appearance of a young brahmin boy.
A single garment was given by me to the Lord of Bipeds, the Tathāgata.
Having accepted that cloth—
The Buddha, the leader supreme in the world,
the Teacher standing in the sky,
spoke these verses.
"By this gift of cloth and by the aspirations of my mind,
having abandoned the womb of a garuḍa,"
"He will delight in the world of the gods.
Then the Blessed One Atthadassī,
the elder of the world, the bull among men;
Having praised the gift of robes,
he departed facing northward as he was being reborn into existence.
I possess an abundance of clothing;
there is a canopy in the sky—
this is the fruit of giving cloth.
Seven men named Aruṇavā,
mighty universal monarchs,
existed during the thirty-sixth [eon].
In this eon, O lords of men,
[I attained] the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, the Venerable Vatthadāyaka Thera indeed recited these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the Venerable Vatthadāyaka Thera.
